meta.title: a clearer first run, a sharper name
meta.description: this week i refreshed onboarding, added subscription access, and gave do or die more polish.

blocks.text: this week was about making do or die feel more understandable from the first screen, rather than asking people to decipher its whole deal through vibes alone.

the app has a fairly direct premise: deadlines should have consequences. but a direct premise can still turn into a confusing first run if the setup, pricing, and everyday screens do not tell the same story.

i shipped a more complete onboarding flow, including a clearer path into the app’s setup and premium access. i also added a paywall with plan selection, purchase restoration, and a place to manage an existing subscription. the boring-but-important part is that the available plans and trial details now come through more reliably, instead of being treated like permanent wall decor.

i refreshed screens outside the admin-oriented areas so the product feels more coherent in normal use. i also added more motion and feedback throughout the experience. not every interaction needs fireworks, but a completely static task app is how you accidentally build a tax form.

i also shipped a weekly summary notification that looks back at missed tasks and time spent under app restrictions. the goal is not to turn sunday evening into a performance review with a tiny angry manager, although it is admittedly adjacent to that.
